research_question: Can a paid local deliverable verification ledger provide two real advantages over free Windows hash and audit tools?

sources.name: hashdeep official manual
observations: Recursive hashing and comparison against saved known hashes are supported
Audit mode reports pass/fail and identifies new or missing files and collisions with verbosity
Manual documents a Unicode filename limitation in audit mode
sources.limitations: Documentation only; no independent Windows install, benchmark, or current Unicode regression test

sources.name: QuickHash GUI official feature page
observations: Free portable Windows GUI hashes files and folders
CSV, HTML and clipboard output are available
Recursive hashing and post-copy verification workflows are advertised
sources.limitations: Vendor claims; actual Windows 11 workflow not independently exercised

sources.name: RapidCRC Unicode official repository
observations: Windows GUI for creating and verifying checksums
Unicode .sha256 and other checksum files with selectable UTF-8/UTF-16 encodings
Shell extension, multithreaded hashing and portable releases advertised
sources.limitations: Repository README only; does not establish snapshot history or human-readable client reports

sources.name: OpenHashTab Japanese software review
observations: Free Windows Explorer hash and comparison integration
Japanese localization and multiple-file hash operations described
sources.limitations: Historical editorial review, not dated Microsoft Store purchaser review or 2026 release QA

competitive_parity.candidate: Hash baseline then re-audit missing/added/changed files
Local Windows GUI with folder/file comparison and report export
Unicode filenames and portable checksum interchange
Nontechnical, dated multi-snapshot narrative with explainable change-only client report

critical_findings: Basic hash auditing, change detection, offline operation and CSV/HTML output are not sufficient to charge for File Integrity Ledger.

hashdeep manual's Unicode limitation may motivate testing Japanese paths, but it does not prove that all modern free tools share the defect; RapidCRC Unicode specifically addresses Unicode checksum handling.
Do not equate a saved hash list with a legally certified audit trail, cryptographic signing, repair, tamper resistance, or provenance.
Existing 100-file and 256 MiB limits could undermine the proposed client-deliverable workflow; any change requires a fresh market-fit decision before commercial feature expansion.
proposed_noncommercial_validation: Recruit five actual Windows users who verify handoff deliverables and record their current free-tool workflow, tasks, completion times and willingness to pay.

Compare the same three named snapshots and change-only reports against hashdeep, QuickHash GUI and RapidCRC on Windows 11 using Japanese Unicode filenames, unreadable files, missing files, symlinks and changed-during-hash files.
Collect ten dated direct Microsoft Store customer review URLs for comparable tools; do not substitute old editorial reviews for Store purchaser feedback.
Test 1024x768 EN/JA UI comprehension and recipient ability to understand a client handoff report without needing hashes.
Require two measured advantages, a directly evidenced competitor complaint solved, a clear one-sentence why-pay, and score >=80 before commercial authorization.
provenance: Public-source desk research performed 2026-10-31; source feature claims are not direct user complaints, purchases, installation tests or commercial proof.
